# SETUP

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r load-libraries}
source("setup.R")
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE)
```

# LOAD DATA

```{r load-water-supplies}
water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE) 
```

```{r load-swi-centroids}
swi_pts <- st_read(here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "swi", "swi_points.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r load-swi-results}
swi_csv <- list.files(
  here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
  pattern    = "swi_exposure.*\\.csv",
  full.names = TRUE
) %>% sort() %>% tail(1)

swi_results <- read_csv(swi_csv)
```

# MAP

Water supply points assigned an SWI exposure value are colored by rank, sized
by coastal weight, and outlined in black. Each is connected by a black line to
the SWI estimation point used to assign its value. SWI points used in the
assignment are colored by their raw Case_C value (no border). Water supplies
more than 50 km from any SWI point are grey with a black border. SWI points
not matched to any water supply are grey.

```{r build-map}
# Join results onto water supply geometries
ws_mapped <- water_supplies %>%
  inner_join(
    swi_results %>% select(-park_unit, -park_name),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  )

# Coastal water supplies only (those with an assigned SWI value)
ws_coastal <- ws_mapped %>%
  filter(!is.na(raw_swi_migration)) %>%
  st_transform(5070)

swi_proj <- st_transform(swi_pts, 5070)

# Find nearest SWI point for each coastal water supply
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(ws_coastal, swi_proj)
used_idx    <- unique(nearest_idx)
swi_used    <- swi_proj[used_idx, ]  %>% st_transform(4326)
swi_unused  <- swi_proj[-used_idx, ] %>% st_transform(4326)

# Build lines connecting each water supply to its matched SWI point
connector_lines <- st_nearest_points(
  ws_coastal,
  swi_proj[nearest_idx, ],
  pairwise = TRUE
) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_transform(4326)

pal <- colorRampPalette(c("green", "yellow", "red"))

# Scale point size by coastal_weight
point_size <- ifelse(
  is.na(ws_mapped$coastal_weight),
  2,
  scales::rescale(ws_mapped$coastal_weight, to = c(3, 8))
)

mapview(swi_unused,
        col.regions = "grey",
        color       = "grey",
        cex         = 4,
        layer.name  = "SWI Points (unused)") +
  mapview(connector_lines,
        color      = "black",
        lwd        = 1,
        layer.name = "WS → SWI connection") +
  mapview(swi_used,
          zcol        = "Case_C",
          col.regions = pal,
          color       = NA,
          cex         = 5,
          pch         = 18,
          layer.name  = "SWI Points (Case_C)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(swi_used) %>%
              select(watershed_id, Case_C)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_mapped,
          zcol        = "rank_swi_migration",
          col.regions = pal,
          na.color    = "grey",
          color       = "black",
          lwd         = 2,
          cex         = point_size,
          layer.name  = "SWI Exposure (rank)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_mapped) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name, raw_swi_migration,
                     norm_swi_migration, rank_swi_migration, coastal_weight)
          ))
```

Browsing this map you will probably immediately find some strange examples. 
Using a 50km buffer around a SWI point to limit the search area for assignment
of the exposure value does not consider the possibility that the closest
value may be on an island just off the coast. Forcing water supplies to 
only use SWI points that are in the same polygon as them still does not
resolve the the issue of SWI assignment crossing channels, and runs into the 
issue of no assignment when the closest SWI point is just off the coast, like 
many of the points on the Cape Cod National Seashore.

You will also notice that there are water supplies that have a coastal weight
but no SWI assignment. That means that during the coastal weighting calculation
they were within 50km of a coastline, but not within 50km of a SWI point.
